claims.text: Conventionally processed metal-based alloys commonly exhibit a trade-off in which increased strength is accompanied by reduced ductility.
Microstructural engineering can produce alloys combining high strength with high tensile ductility.
A multi-parameter machine-learning framework will identify thermo-mechanical processing conditions that overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
Machine-learning predictions can guide the selection of annealing temperature, strain rate, and cooling profile to form desired microstructural features.
A hierarchical microstructure combining refined grains with controlled coherent precipitates can simultaneously improve strength and ductility.
Refined grain size is a necessary component of the proposed strength-ductility synergy.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve local stress concentrations that could otherwise initiate premature cracking.
A fine microstructure containing alternating soft FCC and hard BCC-related phases can provide high fracture strength and high tensile ductility.
Machine-learning-guided optimization of processing conditions alters defect distributions.
Machine-learning-guided optimization of processing conditions alters phase morphologies.
The optimized defect distributions and phase morphologies enable the simultaneous activation of transformation-induced plasticity and twin-induced plasticity.
Transformation-induced plasticity and twin-induced plasticity alleviate stress concentrations while maintaining high strength.
Machine-learning-guided thermo-mechanical processing will yield a simultaneous measurable increase in tensile strength and ductility relative to conventional processing.
The effectiveness of the proposed method depends on alloy composition and training-data quality.
The magnitude of any simultaneous strength and ductility improvement remains uncertain and requires experimental validation.
